newsitem.title: USA: CME pork bellies end limit up, hogs mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: CME pork bellies end limit up, hogs mostly higher.

text.p: A lack of deliveries against the July pork belly futures and talk of bottoming action in cash belly prices boosted July CME pork belly futures up the limit at the close, traders said.
Hog futures generally posted gains on expected firmer cash hog markets, traders said.

Pork bellies closed up the 3.000-cent-per-lb daily limit in July at 81.675 cents while other months ended up 2.375 to unchanged with August up 2.375 at 79.875 cents. Hog futures finished 0.425 cent a lb higher to 0.325 lower with August up 0.075 at 80.725 cents.
Pork bellies ran up on light deliveries against futures and talk that cash belly prices may be approaching a near-term bottom after a several day slide, they said.

Deliveries have been much lighter than expected and are being stopped by strong hands. This added to expectations the cash market is near a bottom after falling $10 per cwt since early last week. An out-movement from Chicago warehouses this week and normal seasonal strength bolstered demand, they said.
"This time of year it's tough to be short those bellies because you have a strong demand typically for bacon during this time frame," said Don Roose, president of U.S. Commodities Inc.
R.J. O'Brien, E.D.&F. Man, Hammer Trading and LFG bought August early and Refco bought late. Locals and R.J. O'Brien sold late. Locals and LFG bought July, pit sources said.

The expected decline in the CME lean hog index kept July hogs under pressure ahead of expiration next Tuesday but other months rose on expectations hot and humid weather, as forecast by some private meteorologists, will support cash hogs into next week. Although packer cutout margins are deep in the red, packers are trying to hold market share and tight hog supplies should keep prices strong, traders said.

Despite some forecasts for heat to return to the Midwest next week, the National Weather Service six- to 10-day forecast issued Wednesday indicated the Midwest will experience below normal temperatures and above normal rainfall for the period July 15-19.
Fund rolling, buying of October and selling of August, limited the gain in August, traders said.

Rand Financials was on both sides of August early and bought late along with locals while selling July and buying October. The "Goldman roll" continued with Refco and Goldman Sachs buying October and selling August, pit sources said.
In hog options, Rand Financials sold December 68 and 70 puts and August 79 and 80 puts. Rosenthal Collins sold August 79 puts while Lind-Waldock sold August 82 calls, pit sources added.
